Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 47, verse 1:

(p-5371) 47. Surat Muhammad

It is named so because it contains the point that belief in what was revealed to Muhammad, sent down piecemeal, is greater than belief in what was revealed in its entirety to the rest of the prophets, peace be upon them. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. It is also called Surat al-Qital (the Chapter of Fighting), because it indicates the lifting of the sanctity of the lives of the disbelievers that would otherwise prevent fighting them, and what follows from fighting and the abundance of its benefits. This is related from al-Mahayimi.

It is a Madani surah. al-Nasafi related a strange opinion that it is Makki. Its number of verses is thirty-eight.

(p-5372) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1] ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah, He will render their deeds void.﴾

﴿Those who disbelieve﴾ means: those who deny the Oneness of Allah and worship other than Him. ﴿And bar (others) from the way of Allah﴾ means: they turn away from and refuse to acknowledge Allah's Oneness and His Messenger's prophethood. Or they bar others from that. ﴿He will render their deeds void﴾ means: He makes them without guidance or right direction.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 47, verse 2:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad – and it is the truth from their Lord – He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition.﴾

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., the acts of obedience between them and their Lord. As for His saying, ﴿and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad﴾, i.e., in what Allah sent down through Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad ﷺ. He specified it by mention, despite its being included in what precedes it, to glorify his station and to instruct; for faith is not valid nor complete except with it. Its conjunction (by 'atf) indicates that it is the greatest of its pillars, due to its being singled out by mention. This is confirmed by the parenthetical clause, which is His saying, ﴿and it is the truth from their Lord﴾, i.e., the established reality and the true state of affairs. ﴿He will remove from them their misdeeds﴾, i.e., He will cover, by their faith and righteous deeds, what was of disbelief and sins on their part, because of their return from them and their repentance. ﴿And amend their condition﴾, i.e., their state and affairs, and their works in this world, with support and success.

Al-Shihab said: (al-bal) may mean "state" and "affair," and it may be specific to a great matter, as in his saying ﷺ, "Every matter of importance (dhi bal)..." It may also mean a "passing thought of the heart," used figuratively for the heart; if it were interpreted this way here, it would also be good. Al-Safaqsi interpreted it as "thought," because when his heart and thought are sound, his belief and actions are sound. Ibn Jarir said: al-bal is like a verbal noun (masdar), like al-sha'n (affair); no verb is derived from it, and the Arabs hardly pluralize it except in poetic necessity; when they do pluralize it, they say "ba'alat."

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying:

[3] ﴿That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to people their parables.﴾

﴿That﴾ means: what is mentioned of His action toward the two groups is what He did, as an occurrence. ﴿Because﴾ means: because of the fact that ﴿those who disbelieved followed falsehood, and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present to people their parables﴾ means: He makes likenesses for them, so that each group is given forms of parables that match them.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, where is the striking of parables? I say: it lies in His making the following of falsehood a parable for the deeds of the disbelievers, and the following of truth a parable for the deeds of the believers. Or it lies in His making misguidance a parable for the disbelievers' failure, and the expiation of evil deeds a parable for the believers' success. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 47, verse 4:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [then] strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, bind [them] firmly. Then either [grant] reward afterwards or ransom until the war lays down its burdens. That [is so]. And if Allah had willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them, but [He ordered war] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - He will never let their deeds be lost.﴾

﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [then] strike [their] necks﴾ Since the opening of this surah served as a preparation for fighting the polytheists who strive in the land with corruption and who bar [others] from the path of righteous guidance, and as an impetus to sincerity (p-5374) in fighting them, to sweep away the obstacle of their falsehood, in acting upon what faith requires and certainty demands, and to distinguish the allies of the Most Merciful from the allies of Satan, that opening was affected by this sentence. Therefore Abu al-Su'ud said: The fa' (then) is for the ordering of what lies within its scope upon what precedes it. The misguidance of the deeds of the disbelievers and their wickedness, and the righteousness of the states of the believers and their success, necessitate that each of the two sides be given the rulings that befit it. That is: if the matter is as has been mentioned, then when you meet them in battle, [then] strike their necks. The original is: "strike the necks, striking." The verb was deleted, the verbal noun was placed first, and it was made to substitute for the verb, being annexed to the object. This involves brevity and emphatic intensification. Expressing killing by this phrase portrays it in its most hideous form, magnifies its matter, and guides the warriors to the easiest way of doing it. ﴿Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them﴾ meaning: you have overpowered them and subdued those among them whose necks you did not strike, so they become captives in your hands. ﴿Then bind [them] firmly﴾ - the word al-wath_q (the bond) is pronounced with a fatḥah on the waw, and it has also been read with a kasrah. It is that by which one is bound, that is, tied and fastened, like a shackle or a rope. That is: hold them with it, lest they kill you and flee from you. ﴿Then either [grant] reward afterwards or ransom﴾ meaning: either you grant them favour after that, releasing them without compensation, because their ferocity has ceased, or you ransom them, releasing them in exchange for property, or for a Muslim whom they captured, so that the Muslims are strengthened by it, or so that their captive is freed.

Al-Mahayimi said: Killing was not mentioned, being sufficient by what has passed in His words: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he inflicts slaughter upon the earth﴾ [al-Anfal: 67]. This is for one who sees that the imam may maintain the ferocity [of the enemy] in its completeness. Enslavement was not mentioned, because it amounts to the continuation of captivity, and this is for one who sees in it a kind of ferocity. And [keep them bound] thus until: ﴿the war lays down its burdens﴾ meaning: until the end of the war. Al-awzār (burdens) are like loads in weight and in meaning. It is borrowed for the instruments of war without which it cannot stand, as a metaphor either explicit or implicit, by likening them to a man carrying a load upon his head or back, and attributing that [carrying] to it by imagination. Its mention has come in the words of al-A'sha:

"And you prepared for war its burdens: long spears and stallion horses."

(p-5375) It was also said: its burdens are its sins, meaning: until the people of war - who are the polytheists - abandon their polytheism and their disobediences by submitting [to Islam].

Remarks:

First: In al-Iklil he said: The verse contains an explanation of the manner of jihad.

Second: The early scholars (al-salaf) have two opinions as to whether the verse is abrogated (mansukh) or non-abrogated (muhkam).

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi that it is abrogated by His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5]. They said: after the disavowal [of treaties] and the passing of the sacred months, no polytheist retains any covenant or protection.

And it is narrated from Ibn 'Umar, 'Ata', al-Hasan, and 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz that the verse is non-abrogated (muhkam), not abrogated, and that it is not permissible to kill a captive; rather, the only [options] for him are favour or ransom.

The basis of those who held the first view is that the two verses contradict each other at first glance, so there remains only the acceptance of one of them, namely the unrestricted one.

The basis of the second view is that the general command to kill them in [other] verses is to be understood in light of the specified case in verses like this one. That is: killing at the time of encounter, and then after the war has ended, favour or ransom only, unless a benefit is seen in killing, in which case that falls under a different category.

There is also a third view: that the verse is non-abrogated while the matter is entrusted to the imam, and that the mention of favour and ransom does not negate the permissibility of killing, since that is known from other verses. This is especially so since the matter ultimately returns to the public interest. This is the view I choose. When the matter of the verses falls between being non-abrogated and being abrogated, the former is the preferred one. The view of those who speak of abrogation may not contradict that of those who hold the verse non-abrogated, because of what we have already presented in the introduction to the tafsir regarding the difference between the terminology of the early scholars and that of the jurists of legal theory (usuliyyun) concerning naskh (abrogation).

(p-5376) Then I saw that Ibn Jarir had preceded me in preferring this view, and his words are:

"The correct view in our opinion regarding this is that this verse is non-abrogated (muhkam) and not abrogated (mansukh). That is because the attribute of the abrogating and the abrogated is that the two rulings cannot be combined in a single state, or that proof has been established that one of them abrogates the other. It is not objectionable that the choice between favour, ransom, and killing has been left to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to those who stand after him in charge of the affairs of the community, even though killing is not mentioned in this verse, because He has already permitted their killing in another verse, which is His words: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], and so on. Indeed, that is so, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to act thus with those among the people of war who became captives in his hand: he would kill some, ransom others, and show favour to others. Such as on the day of Badr: he killed 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it when he had been brought to him as a captive. He killed the Banu Qurayzah after they had descended to the judgment of Sa'd, and they had come into his hand in submission, while he was able to ransom them or show favour to them. He ransomed a group of the polytheist captives who had been captured at Badr, and he showed favour to Thumamah ibn Uthal al-Hanafi while he was a captive in his hand. This continued to be established from his conduct toward the people of war from the time Allah permitted him to fight them until He took him to Himself (ﷺ); it was always so with them. Mighty is His praise, in this verse He mentioned favour and ransom concerning the captives and specified their mention here, because the command to kill them and the permission for that had already been repeated in the other verses of His revelation. So He informed His Prophet (ﷺ) through what He mentioned in this verse of favour and ransom, what he had regarding them alongside killing." End of Ibn Jarir's words.

Third: Among the benefits of the verse is also the permissibility of releasing the polytheists when their strength has weakened and their mischief is secure, because that is among the necessary consequences of showing favour and accepting ransom. The view of exterminating their population without detail is contradicted by the explicit text of this verse, and by the Prophet's (ﷺ) acceptance of the jizyah (poll tax) from the Magians of Hajar, who were polytheists. So understand this.

(p-5377) In sum, what the scrupulous imams - may Allah be pleased with them - rely upon is that the commander, after gaining victory, is given the choice, out of consideration for public interest and not desire, regarding the captive fighters, between killing and enslavement, and between favour and ransom. He is obliged to choose what is most beneficial for the Muslims, because he acts on their behalf with a view to their welfare, so it is not permissible for him to abandon what holds the greater benefit, like the guardian of an orphan. This is because each of these options may be the most beneficial for some captives. Among them is one who has strength and power against the Muslims, so killing him is most beneficial. Among them is the weak one with much wealth, so his ransom is most beneficial. Among them is one who holds a good opinion of the Muslims and whose conversion is hoped for, so favour toward him is preferable. And one from whom benefit can be gained through service, and whose evil is secure, his enslavement is most beneficial, as in Sharh al-Iqna' (Commentary on al-Iqna').

Fourth: It is recommended to invite the disbelievers to Islam before fighting, for whoever has received the call, in order to cut off their argument. It is forbidden to fight before it for whoever has not received the call, based on the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) appointed a commander over a detachment or an army, he would instruct him to fear Allah, the Exalted, regarding his own person and regarding the Muslims with him. He said: 'When you meet your enemy from among the polytheists, invite them to one of three things. If they respond to you with any of them, accept it from them and refrain from them: invite them to Islam; if they respond, accept it from them and refrain from them. If they refuse, invite them to give the jizyah; if they respond, accept it from them and refrain from them. If they refuse, seek help from Allah and fight them.'" Related by Muslim.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim restricted the obligation and the recommendation of the call to the case in which the Muslims intend them. As for when the disbelievers intend to fight the Muslims, then the Muslims may fight them without a call, to repel [the attack] from their souls and their sanctuary. The matter of jihad is entrusted to the imam and his judgment, because he knows best the condition of the people, the condition of the enemy, their strength, their proximity, and their distance, as in Sharh al-Iqna'.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿That [is so]﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: the matter is that. Or it is the object of an implied verb: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them﴾ meaning: He would have punished them with a swift punishment and spared you all of that. ﴿But [He ordered war] to test some of you by means of others﴾ (p-5378) meaning: to test you through them, so that He may know the mujahidun among you and the patient ones, and reward them, and to test them through you, so that He punishes whom He wills of them by your hands until they turn back to the truth. ﴿And those who are killed﴾ meaning: those who are martyred. It has also been read as qatalū (fought): ﴿in the cause of Allah - He will never let their deeds be lost.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 47, verses 5–6:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[5–6] ﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs﴾ ﴿and admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad: 6].

﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs﴾ ﴿and admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad: 6]. That is: He made it clear to them in many of His verses, in a manner of description that makes every believer eager to strive for it.

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[5–6] ﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs﴾ ﴿and admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad: 6].

﴿He will guide them and set right their affairs﴾ ﴿and admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them﴾ [Muhammad: 6]. That is: He made it clear to them in many of His verses, in a manner of description that makes every believer eager to strive for it.

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.﴾ That is: victory and establishment in the land, and inheritance of the abodes of the enemy.

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[8–9] ﴿As for those who disbelieve, ruin is theirs, and He will make their deeds go astray.﴾ ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah has sent down, so He has nullified their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 9].

﴿As for those who disbelieve, ruin is theirs﴾, i.e., disgrace and misery. Its origin is falling on the face, like being overturned (al-kabb). ﴿And He will make their deeds go astray﴾, i.e., He made them not upon guidance and uprightness. ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah has sent down﴾ [Muhammad: 9], i.e., of the truth, and they followed what they had fabricated of falsehood. ﴿So He has nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 9], like their worship of their idols, since it did not benefit them. Rather, it destroyed them, so they roasted in the blaze.

(p-٥٣٧٩)

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? God destroyed them utterly, and for the disbelievers there are similar consequences.﴾

﴿Have they not travelled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ That is, of the nations that denied their messengers and rejected their counsel. ﴿God destroyed them utterly﴾ That is, He destroyed what was specific to them and belonged to them. It is said: "dammara-hu" (dammarahu) means "he destroyed it," while "dammara 'alayhi" (dammara ʿalayhi) means "he destroyed what belonged to him of wealth and person." The second is more emphatic, because of the generality it carries, since its object becomes a forgotten thing (nasyan mansiyyan), so it encompasses himself and everything that belongs to him. The use of "ʿalā" (ʿala, "upon") is because it implies the meaning of "ṭabaqa ʿalayhi" (it overwhelmed him), that is, He brought it down upon them, encompassing them, or destruction swooped down upon them. ﴿And for the disbelievers﴾ meaning those who denied the Messenger of God (ﷺ): ﴿similar consequences﴾ That is, the like of the consequence of the denial of the earlier nations.

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. As for those who disbelieve, they enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode.﴾ [Muhammad: 11–12]

﴿That is because Allah is the Protector of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector.﴾ That is: they have no helper who can ward off the punishment from them when it befalls them. ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. As for those who disbelieve, they enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat.﴾ [Muhammad: 12] That is: they are not reflecting on the return (al-Ma'ad) and are not taking warning from the established way (Sunnah) of Allah, like the heedlessness of livestock regarding slaughter and sacrifice. So their only concern is grazing (al-i'tilaf) and nothing beyond it. ﴿And the Fire is their abode.﴾ [Muhammad: 12] That is: their dwelling place after their death.

(p-٥٣٨٠)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[13–14] ﴿And how many a town, more powerful than your town which expelled you, have We destroyed, with none to help them.﴾ ﴿Is one who stands on clear evidence from his Lord like one whose evil deeds have been made attractive to him, and who follow their desires?﴾ [Muhammad: 14].

﴿وكَأيِّنْ﴾ means "and how many" (وكَمْ). ﴿From a town which is stronger in power than your town which expelled you﴾ refers to Makkah, with an omitted modifier (ḥadhf muḍāf, the ellipsis of a noun governing the genitive): the meaning is "the people of" the town. ﴿We destroyed them, and they had no helper.﴾

﴿Is one who stands on clear evidence from his Lord﴾ [Muhammad: 14], i.e., on proof, argument, and clarity from his Lord's command and knowledge of His oneness, so he worships Him with insight from Him. ﴿Like one whose evil deeds have been made attractive to him﴾ [Muhammad: 14], i.e., Satan showed it to him as good, so he persists in it. ﴿And who follow their desires.﴾ [Muhammad: 14]

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[13–14] ﴿And how many a town, more powerful than your town which expelled you, have We destroyed, with none to help them.﴾ ﴿Is one who stands on clear evidence from his Lord like one whose evil deeds have been made attractive to him, and who follow their desires?﴾ [Muhammad: 14].

﴿وكَأيِّنْ﴾ means "and how many" (وكَمْ). ﴿From a town which is stronger in power than your town which expelled you﴾ refers to Makkah, with an omitted modifier (ḥadhf muḍāf, the ellipsis of a noun governing the genitive): the meaning is "the people of" the town. ﴿We destroyed them, and they had no helper.﴾

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿The likeness of the Garden promised to the God-fearing: in it are rivers of water unchanging, and rivers of milk whose taste never alters, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink, and rivers of clarified honey. For them therein is every kind of fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord. Are they like one who abides in the Fire and is given boiling water to drink, which cuts their bowels to pieces?﴾

﴿The likeness of the Garden promised to the God-fearing: in it are rivers of water unchanging﴾, i.e., whose smell has not changed. ﴿And rivers of milk whose taste has not altered, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink, and rivers of clarified honey﴾, i.e., free from impurities, unlike the honey of this world. ﴿For them therein is every kind of fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord. Are they like one who abides in the Fire and is given boiling water to drink, which cuts their bowels to pieces﴾, i.e., because of its extreme heat.

(p-5381) A subtle point (lata'if):

﴿The likeness of the Garden﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is ﴿like one who abides﴾, with an implied interrogative particle of denial (harf inkar) and an implied noun: that is, "Is the likeness of the people of the Garden like the likeness of one who abides [in the Fire]?" Or: "Is the likeness of the Garden like the recompense of one who abides [in the Fire]?" Although the wording of the verse is in affirmative form, its meaning is one of denial and negation, because it falls under the rule of a statement introduced by the particle of denial and its governing force extends to it, namely His saying ﴿Is one who ... [14]﴾ and so on. There is no verbal indicator of this in the wording; it is drawn from the context, and in it lies the eloquence (jaza'lah) of the meaning. There are other grammatical analyses (i'rab) as well, but this is the strongest of them.

The commentary on His words, may He be exalted:

[16] ﴿And among them are some who listen to you, until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and they follow their own desires.﴾

﴿And among them﴾ i.e., among these disbelievers: ﴿some﴾ i.e., a disbeliever, a hypocrite: ﴿who listen to you, until, when they go out from your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge﴾ i.e., from among the Companions, mockingly, regarding what they had heard of the recited words, and dismissively: ﴿"What did he just say?"﴾ i.e., a moment ago. Is there any guidance in it? If they explain it, they gain nothing from it. ﴿Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal﴾ i.e., so guidance does not enter them, because of their refusal to accept it. ﴿And they follow their own desires﴾ i.e., their opinions, not what proof calls for.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿And those who are guided — He increases them in guidance and bestows upon them their God-consciousness.﴾

﴿And those who are guided﴾ means: by following the truth and walking with the proof. ﴿He increases them in guidance﴾ means: He gives them clarity regarding the reality of what has come to them. ﴿And bestows upon them their God-consciousness﴾ means: He helps them to attain it. Or: He bestows upon them the reward of their God-consciousness, or He makes clear to them what they should guard against.

(p-5382)

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, statement:

[18] ﴿Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come. So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾.

﴿Are they waiting for anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly? Its signs have already come﴾. Ibn Kathir said: That is, the indicators (ashrat) of its approach, as in His, the Blessed and Exalted, statement: ﴿This is a warner of the warners of old﴾ [An-Najm: 56] ﴿The imminent approaches﴾ [An-Najm: 57], and as in His, the Majestic and Most High, statement: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [Al-Qamar: 1], and His, the Glorified and Exalted, statement: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [An-Nahl: 1], and His, the Majestic and Most High, statement: ﴿The reckoning has drawn near for the people, while they are heedless and turning away﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 1]. Thus the sending of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among the signs of the Hour, because he is the seal of the messengers, through whom Allah, the Exalted, completed the religion and established the proof against all the worlds. He (ﷺ) informed of the signs of the Hour and its indicators, and clarified and explained them, in a manner that no prophet before him was given, as is expounded in its proper place.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) is among the signs of the Hour, and he spoke the truth. For this reason, it has been reported among his (ﷺ) names that he is the Prophet of Repentance, the Prophet of the Great Battle, the Hashir (the one at whose feet people will be gathered), and the Aqib (the one after whom there is no prophet).

Al-Bukhari reported from Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, while indicating with his two fingers in this way, the middle finger and the one next to it: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two."

﴿So how will they have their reminder when it comes to them?﴾. That is, the remembrance of what they neglected and fell short in of obedience to Allah when the Hour comes upon them. The meaning is that it is not a time in which remembrance and regret will benefit them, because it is a time of recompense, not a time of making amends (isti'tab) or of performing deeds (isti'mal).

(p-٥٣٨٣)

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[19] ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows your moving about and your resting place.﴾

﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah﴾. Ibn Jarir said: That is, know, O Muhammad, that there is no worshipped one who is fit or suitable to be given divinity, and whom it is permissible for you and for creation to worship, except Allah, who is the Creator of creation and the Owner of everything. Everything other than Him submits to Him in lordship. The fa' (so) here is fasihah (an eloquent connective particle) in answer to a known condition, derived from what has passed from the beginning of the surah until here, concerning the state of the two groups.

Al-Suyuti said: The verse has been used as evidence by those who hold that reflective inquiry (nazar) is obligatory and that blind imitation (taqlid) in matters of belief is invalid, and by those who hold that the first of the obligations is knowledge (ma'rifah) before affirmation (iqrar).

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾. Ibn Jarir said: That is, and ask your Lord for forgiveness of the sins you committed in the past and those you commit in the present, and the sins of the people of faith in you, both men and women. Al-Shihab said: The preposition (li) was repeated because their sins are a different kind from the sin of the Prophet ﷺ, for their sins are acts of disobedience, both major and minor, whereas his sin is the leaving of the better course (tark al-awla).

Al-Suyuti said: Those who permit minor sins for the prophets have used this verse as evidence. End of quotation.

The matter is set out at length with its positions, and what is for and against it, in (al-Fasl) by Ibn Hazm, so refer to it.

In the Sahih it is related that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "O Allah, forgive me my error and my ignorance, and my excess in my affairs, and that which You know better than I. O Allah, forgive me my jest and my earnestness, my errors and my deliberate faults, and all of that is with me."

In the Sahih it is also related that he used to say at the end of the prayer: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public, my excess, and that which You know better than I. You are my God; there is no deity except You."

In the Sahih it is related that he said: "O people! Repent to your Lord, for I seek forgiveness from Allah and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day."

﴿And Allah knows your moving about and your resting place﴾. That is, your movement in what you move about in, and your staying in what you stay upon, of sayings and deeds, and He will recompense you for it.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[20] ﴿Those who believe say, "Why has no surah been sent down?" But when a clear surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you with the look of one who has fainted from death. So woe to them.﴾

﴿Those who believe say, "Why has no surah been sent down?"﴾ That is: they say, "Why does it not command us to fight the enemies of Allah among the disbelievers?" ﴿But when a clear surah is sent down﴾ That is: explicit, admitting neither abrogation (naskh) nor reinterpretation (ta'wil), ﴿and fighting is mentioned in it﴾, that is, the command to fight the polytheists, ﴿you see those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ That is: doubt regarding the religion and weakness of certainty. ﴿Looking at you with the look of one who has fainted from death﴾ That is: out of their alarm, terror, and cowardice at meeting the enemies. He likened their gaze to the gaze of the dying person whose eyes do not blink. (p-5385) ﴿So woe to them (fa-awla lahum)﴾. Al-Shihab said: There is disagreement concerning it, although there is agreement that its intended meaning is threat and warning, and there are several opinions:

Al-Asma'i held that it is a past-tense verb (fi'l madi) meaning "came near" (qaraba). It was said: it is qarraba with the doubled letter, so its subject is a pronoun referring to what is known from the context, meaning: their destruction drew near. Most scholars hold that it is an elative noun (ism tafdil) derived from al-wali, in the sense of "nearness." Abu 'Ali said: it is an elative noun derived from al-wayl (woe). The original form would be awyal, which was transposed, so its pattern is afla'. This was refuted on the grounds that wayl is not inflected, and that transposition is contrary to the original form, though there is room for consideration. It has also been said that it is fa'la, derived from aala yu'awilu. Al-Radi said: it is a proper noun functioning as a threat, and it is the subject (mubtada'), with lahum as its predicate. It has been heard with a feminine ending as ulaah. As has been said, this indicates that it is neither an elative (af'al tafdil) nor an af'al-fu'la form, that it is a proper noun and not a verb, but rather like armal and armala when named with them, which is why it is not inflected. Nor is it an imperative-type noun (ism fi'l), because it has been heard inflected in the nominative (marfu'an), and had it been an ism fi'l it would have been indeclinable. In this there is the point that there is no obstacle to awla being a different word with the same meaning, so nothing of this objection applies to them at all, just as awwal came as an elative noun and as a noun of time, like qabl. It has also been heard as ulah, as Abu Hayyan transmitted, so the objection of deficiency does not arise from it, as is not hidden. End of quotation.

Al-Samin said: If we say that it is a noun, then there are several possibilities:

The first: it is the subject (mubtada'), and lahum is its predicate; its estimated sense is: so destruction is for them.

The second: it is the predicate of an implied subject; its estimated sense is: punishment or destruction is more fitting for them (awla lahum), that is, closer and nearer. It is also permissible that the lam carries the sense of the ba', meaning: more fitting and more deserving for them.

The third: it is the subject, and lahum is attached to it, with the lam carrying the sense of the ba', and ta'a (obedience) is its predicate. The estimated sense is: so obedience is more fitting for them, rather than anything else. And His saying, exalted is He:

(p-5386) The discussion of the Exalted's words:

[21] ﴿Obedience and fair speech. So when the matter is resolved upon, if they had been true to God, it would have been better for them.﴾

Regarding ﴿obedience and fair speech﴾ there are several views:

First: it is the predicate (*khabar*, the complement of the subject) of "*awlā*" (the phrase "*awlā lahum*"), as already mentioned.

Second: it is a description (*ṣifah*, adjective) of the surah, meaning: when a decisive surah is revealed, [it is] obedience, i.e., possessing obedience, or obeyed. This was mentioned by Makki and Abu al-Baqa'. But it is remote, because of the many intervening words.

Third: it is the subject (*mubtada'*), with "*qawl*" (speech) conjoined to it, and the predicate is omitted. Its estimate is: "They are better for you than those two." Makki estimated it as: "From us is obedience," thus placing it as a fronted predicate.

Fourth: it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "Our matter is obedience."

Fifth: "*lahum*" (for them) is a fronted predicate, and "*ṭā'ah*" (obedience) is a postponed subject. The pause and the beginning are known from what I have already set forth, so reflect on it. (Related by al-Samin.)

﴿So when the matter is resolved upon﴾, i.e., the situation became serious and fighting was present. Abu al-Su'ud said: he attributed resolve, which is earnestness, to the matter, while it belongs to its people, metaphorically, as in the Exalted's words: ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters requiring resolve﴾ [Luqman: 17]. The governing element of the adverbial phrase is omitted, meaning: they opposed and held back. It was said: they broke their word. It was said: they disliked it. It was said: the ﴿if they had been true to God﴾ is according to the manner of your saying: "When food is present to me, if you came to me, I would feed you." That is: if they had been true to Him, the Exalted, in what they said, of the speech that indicates eagerness for jihad, by acting upon its requirement: ﴿it would have been better for them﴾, i.e., the truth would have been better for them, in the immediate affairs of their worldly life and the later outcome of their return. It was said: if they had been true to Him in faith, and their hearts had agreed with their tongues in that. In any case, the intended ones are those in whose hearts is a disease, and they are the ones addressed by the Exalted's words:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22] ﴿Then, is it possible that if you turn away, you would cause corruption on the earth and sever your ties of kinship?﴾

﴿Then, is it possible that if you turn away﴾ means: if you turn away from the revelation of God, exalted is He, and depart from the rulings of His Book and what His Messenger brought. ﴿That you would cause corruption on the earth﴾, meaning through mutual raiding and plundering, ﴿and sever your ties of kinship﴾ (p-5387), meaning: you would return to what you were upon in your pre-Islamic ignorance of scattering and division, after God had united you through Islam, joined your hearts by it, and commanded you to make peace on the earth and to maintain ties of kinship. Maintaining ties of kinship is doing good to relatives in speech and deeds, and giving them of one's wealth. Here Ibn Kathir has cited, regarding the maintenance of ties of kinship, the essence of the essences of the hadiths.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[23] ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf and blinded their vision.﴾

﴿Those﴾ refers to those previously mentioned. ﴿Whom Allah has cursed, so He has made them deaf﴾, that is, deaf to hearing the truth, because they made themselves deaf to it through their own wrong choice. ﴿And blinded their vision﴾, that is, because they blinded themselves to the signs that they see, which are set out in the souls (anfus) and the horizons (afaq).

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[24] ﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, will these hypocrites not reflect upon the admonitions of God with which He admonishes them in the verses of the Qur'an that He sent down to His Prophet, peace be upon him, and contemplate His proofs which He made clear to them in His revelation, so that they might know by them the error of what they persist in? ﴿Or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ That is, no remembrance reaches them and no matter is disclosed to them. The indefiniteness of (hearts) indicates the extreme of their ignorance and strangeness, as if they were obscure and unknown. And (locks) is a metaphor for whatever prevents access. Its being attributed to the hearts serves to specify that it is exclusive to them, distinguishing it from anything else, and to indicate that these locks are not like the familiar locks, since they can never be opened.

(p-5388)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[25] ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them — Satan has enticed them and given them false hope.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels﴾ means: they returned to what they had been upon of disbelief. ﴿After guidance had become clear to them﴾ means: the truth, with its evident proof. ﴿Satan has enticed them﴾ means: he made their apostasy seem attractive to them and drove them to it. ﴿And given them false hope﴾ means: he extended to them hopes and wishful expectations. Or it means: Allah, exalted is He, granted them respite, so He prolonged their lifespans and did not hasten punishment upon them. The meaning is: Satan enticed them, and Allah granted them respite.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah has sent down: "We will obey you in some matters." But Allah knows their secret conspiring.﴾

﴿That﴾ refers to what was mentioned of their apostasy (irtidad). ﴿Because they﴾ means: because of the fact that they ﴿said﴾, that is, the hypocrites (munafiqun), ﴿to those who hated what Allah has sent down﴾, that is, to the Jews who hated the descent of the Qur'an upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿"We will obey you in some matters"﴾, that is, some of your affairs, or what you command, such as staying back from jihad, colluding against the Messenger, or going out with them if they are expelled. This is clarified by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Book: "If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you"?﴾ [al-Hashr: 11]. They were the Banu Qurayza and the Banu al-Nadir, who used to befriend and show affection to them. ﴿But Allah knows their secret conspiring﴾, that is, their concealing of what they say to the Jews.

(p. 5389)

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[27–28] ﴿How then, when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ ﴿That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 28].

﴿How then﴾ means: what will they do, and how will they ward off the harm of apostasy upon themselves? ﴿When the angels take their souls, striking their faces﴾ means: the faces which they turned away from Allah toward His enemies. ﴿And their backs﴾ means: the backs which they turned away from the enemies toward Allah. ﴿That﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: this terrible taking of souls. ﴿Because they followed what angered Allah﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: by obeying His enemies. ﴿And disliked His pleasure﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: in their opposition to Him, which led them to apostasy. ﴿So He nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: those deeds which would have brought them salvation from that striking and from worldly disgrace.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[27–28] ﴿How then, when the angels take their souls, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ ﴿That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 28].

﴿How then﴾ means: what will they do, and how will they ward off the harm of apostasy upon themselves? ﴿When the angels take their souls, striking their faces﴾ means: the faces which they turned away from Allah toward His enemies. ﴿And their backs﴾ means: the backs which they turned away from the enemies toward Allah. ﴿That﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: this terrible taking of souls. ﴿Because they followed what angered Allah﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: by obeying His enemies. ﴿And disliked His pleasure﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: in their opposition to Him, which led them to apostasy. ﴿So He nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 28] means: those deeds which would have brought them salvation from that striking and from worldly disgrace.

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[29] ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will never bring out their resentments?﴾

﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ — i.e., hypocrisy from which resentments branch out against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers. ﴿That Allah will never bring out﴾ — i.e., will not make manifest — ﴿their resentments﴾ — i.e., their enmities toward His Messenger and the believers, so that their affairs remain concealed. The meaning is that this is something that hardly falls within the realm of possibility.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[30–31] ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would surely recognize them by their marks. And you will certainly know them by the tenor of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the steadfast, and We will test your reports.﴾ [Muhammad: 31]

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you﴾: that is, We would have made you know them by signs, so that you would recognize them by their very persons, with a knowledge that closely approaches sight. ﴿Then you would have recognized them by their marks﴾: that is, by their mark with which We brand them. ﴿And you will certainly know them by the tenor of their speech﴾: that is, by its style (uslub) and by what they say, without explicit clarity about it.

Al-Qasimi said in *al-Iklil*: Whoever holds that allusion to slander (ta'ridh bi-l-qadhf) requires the prescribed punishment (hadd) has taken evidence from this verse.

﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾: that is, He will recompense you according to your intentions. ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the steadfast﴾ [Muhammad: 31]: that is, the people who strive in the way of Allah and endure hardships. ﴿And We will test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]: that is, the varieties of your statements, the kinds of your expressions, and the works of the power of your tongues in spreading the truth, proclaiming it, and persisting in it, whether this is purely for that sake or whether there is in it some of the favouritism that fears the blame of the blamer.

Al-Qashani said: The knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is of two kinds. The first precedes its objects (ma'lumat) in general, in the Preserved Tablet (lawh al-qada', the Tablet of Decree), and in detail in the Tablet of Destiny (lawh al-qadar, the Tablet of Divine Measure). It follows them in their detailed manifestations among human souls and among the particular celestial souls. Thus the meaning of ﴿until We know﴾ [Muhammad: 31] is: until Our detailed knowledge becomes manifest in the manifestations of the angelic realm and of humankind, through which the recompense is established. And Allah knows best.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[30–31] ﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would surely recognize them by their marks. And you will certainly know them by the tenor of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the steadfast, and We will test your reports.﴾ [Muhammad: 31]

﴿And if We willed, We would have shown them to you﴾: that is, We would have made you know them by signs, so that you would recognize them by their very persons, with a knowledge that closely approaches sight. ﴿Then you would have recognized them by their marks﴾: that is, by their mark with which We brand them. ﴿And you will certainly know them by the tenor of their speech﴾: that is, by its style (uslub) and by what they say, without explicit clarity about it.

Al-Qasimi said in *al-Iklil*: Whoever holds that allusion to slander (ta'ridh bi-l-qadhf) requires the prescribed punishment (hadd) has taken evidence from this verse.

﴿And Allah knows your deeds﴾: that is, He will recompense you according to your intentions. ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the steadfast﴾ [Muhammad: 31]: that is, the people who strive in the way of Allah and endure hardships. ﴿And We will test your reports﴾ [Muhammad: 31]: that is, the varieties of your statements, the kinds of your expressions, and the works of the power of your tongues in spreading the truth, proclaiming it, and persisting in it, whether this is purely for that sake or whether there is in it some of the favouritism that fears the blame of the blamer.

Al-Qashani said: The knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, is of two kinds. The first precedes its objects (ma'lumat) in general, in the Preserved Tablet (lawh al-qada', the Tablet of Decree), and in detail in the Tablet of Destiny (lawh al-qadar, the Tablet of Divine Measure). It follows them in their detailed manifestations among human souls and among the particular celestial souls. Thus the meaning of ﴿until We know﴾ [Muhammad: 31] is: until Our detailed knowledge becomes manifest in the manifestations of the angelic realm and of humankind, through which the recompense is established. And Allah knows best.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[32] ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them will never harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds null.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them will never harm Allah at all, and He will render their deeds null.﴾ That is: they will go to waste (suda), yielding no benefit for them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 47, verses 33–34:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33–34] ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – Allah will not forgive them.﴾ [Muhammad: 34]

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – Allah will not forgive them.﴾ [Muhammad: 34] That is: rather, He will punish them and chastise them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 47, verses 33–34:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[33–34] ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – Allah will not forgive them.﴾ [Muhammad: 34]

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – Allah will not forgive them.﴾ [Muhammad: 34] That is: rather, He will punish them and chastise them.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Saying, Exalted is He:

[35] ﴿So do not weaken and call for peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you, and He will not deprive you of your deeds.﴾

﴿So do not weaken﴾ means: do not be feeble, O believers in Allah, in fighting those who have transgressed against you and barred others from the path of Allah. ﴿And call for peace﴾, i.e., reconciliation (al-sulh) and mutual peace-making. ﴿While you are the superior﴾, i.e., the victors. For the sweeping away of misguidance from the path of truth has no escape, so long as its means are available and its adherents are subdued. ﴿And Allah is with you﴾, i.e., with His help, as long as you hold fast to His rope. ﴿And He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, i.e., He will not diminish their reward for you or waste it.

[36] ﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement; and if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards, and He will not ask you for your wealth.﴾

﴿The life of this world is but play and amusement.﴾ That is: let not your desire for life keep you from abandoning jihad. ﴿And if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards.﴾ That is: the reward of your faith and your piety. ﴿And He will not ask you for your wealth.﴾ That is: because He is free of need of you. He only wants from you monotheism (tawhid), the rejection of idols, and obedience to what He has commanded and forbidden.

(p-5392) Some exegetes said: that is, He will not ask for all of your wealth, but will limit Himself to a small part of it, such as a quarter of a tenth or a tenth. This points to the plural noun in construct (al-jam' al-mudaf) conveying a known referent (li-l-ma'lum), and it is coordinated with the conditional response. The meaning is: if you believe, He will not ask for all of it, that is, He will not take it from you as He takes all the wealth of the unbelievers. The fine contrast with His saying ﴿He will give you your rewards﴾ is not hidden; that is, He gives you all the rewards and asks for some of the wealth. This is what al-Shihab (al-Shihab al-Khafaji) said.

The apparent meaning is that the purpose is to show His independence from His servants, and that the request for them to spend their wealth is for its benefit returning to them and not to Him, since He is absolutely free of need. For in charity there is the removal of resentment from the hearts of the poor toward them, and in spending for jihad there is the averting of the harm of evil and corruption. All of this brings its fruit back to them.

Then Exalted is He pointed to His wisdom and His mercy in not asking them to spend all of their wealth, by His saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[37] ﴿If He should ask you for it and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your rancor.﴾

﴿If He should ask you for it and press you, you would be stingy﴾ That is: if He were to burden you with the request and insist upon you to give it to Him, you would be stingy with it and refuse it, out of your miserliness toward it. But He knew this about you, and about the narrowness of your souls, so He did not ask you for it.

Al-Zamakhshari said: al-ihfa' (ihfa', "pressing") means exaggeration and reaching the utmost limit in anything. It is said: "ahfahu fi al-mas'alah" (he pressed him in the request) when he leaves out no degree of insistence; and "ahfa sharibahu" (he shaved his moustache) when he uproots it.

﴿and He would bring out your rancor﴾ That is: your resentments, and your dislike of a religious obligation that would take away your wealth. The pronoun in (yukhrij, "He brings out") refers to Allah, Exalted, and this is supported by the reading with the nun of majesty (nunation of greatness). Or it refers to stinginess, because it is the cause of rancor. It was also read as (yakhruj, "it comes out") from al-khuruj (coming out), with the ya' and the ta', with (al-adghan, "the rancors") as its subject.

(p-5393) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[38] ﴿Here you are, you who are called to spend in the way of Allah; yet among you are those who are stingy. And whoever is stingy is only stingy toward himself. And Allah is the Rich, while you are the poor. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and then they will not be like you.﴾

﴿Here you are, you who are called to spend in the way of Allah﴾, that is, in striving against His enemies and supporting His religion. ﴿Yet among you are those who are stingy﴾, that is, with spending in it. ﴿And whoever is stingy is only stingy toward himself﴾, that is, he withholds it from himself, because he deprives it of the reward and earns for it the burden of sin. ﴿And Allah is the Rich﴾, that is, Independent of everything other than Himself, and everything that is poor is in need of Him. For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿while you are the poor﴾, that is, essentially in need of Him. His being described as Rich is a necessary attribute of Him, and the creatures' being described as poor is a necessary attribute of them; they never separate from it. That is, since this is the case, your urging to spend in His way is only so that He may reward you thereby with His abundant reward, and so that you know that the way of Allah encompasses everything that contains benefit, good, advantage, nearness to Allah, and reward. The exegetes restricted it to striving only because it is its most prominent instance and its most important part at the time the verses were revealed, but it is not confined to it.

﴿And if you turn away﴾, that is, from what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought you: ﴿He will replace you with another people﴾, that is, He will destroy you and then bring other people besides you in your place, who believe in him and act according to his laws.

﴿Then they will not be like you﴾, that is, they will not be stingy with what they have been commanded regarding spending in the way of Allah, nor will they neglect any part of the limits of their religion; rather, they will fulfill all of that as they are commanded.
